theater: 洹水下游（河北磁州安陽間）

battle.name: 洹水之戰
battle.theater: 洹水下游（河北磁州安陽間）
battle.brief: 建中三年（782），成德軍節度使李寶臣拒絕入朝，河北諸鎮皆不奉詔，唐廷以昭義軍節度使張瓊為招討使，會河中諸道兵討之。官軍東出太行、進至洹水一線，與成德軍騎兵接戰失利，朝廷首次削藩落空，轉為招撫。卡面的羅馬標槍未隨軍而至，其空心槍幹受撞即折的用法與唐軍的床弩齊射全然不同。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 洹水之戰是唐廷與成德軍藩鎮在河北南部的一次正面交鋒，雙方的國家形態、軍隊編制與指揮系統幾乎完全相反。中唐名義上的中央政府由德宗控制兩京與關中，可用兵源、財力與合法調兵的空間卻都受藩鎮掣肘：調兵須靠奏請節度使、各道自備兵糧的體例，朝廷能直接指揮的只有關中宿衛與少數京畿部隊，河北的戰事只能倚賴河東、河北各道節度使自領本部兵赴援。河北方面，成德軍節度使李寶臣以恆州為治，節度使衙署與州縣兩套政權並存，自置官吏、徵收賦稅、蓄養牙兵，節度使本人對軍府有近乎專制的支配權，這正是唐中葉藩鎮兵權、財賦與官吏三權合一的典型。與成德互為犄角的魏博、幽州、淄青諸鎮同處河北，全都拒絕朝廷的宣詔，河北諸州實質上成了一片只向節度使負責的兵源與賦稅地帶。李寶臣起兵後，朝廷以河北招討使的名義集合昭義軍節度使張瓊所部以及河中、忠武等處調來的兵力，指揮上卻是各道兵自將、各自為戰，沒有統一作戰計畫與專一的戰場指揮權；河北方面除成德本軍，還有鄰州郡縣的團練、義軍與城守部隊可以徵發。兩相比較，唐軍有編制、有名分而無協同，成德軍有騎兵、有城寨而無外援節制，這正是洹水一役的結構性前提。
countriesEn: The Battle of Huanshui was a direct clash between the Tang court and the Chengde military governorship in southern Hebei, and the two sides had almost opposite state forms, force structures and command systems. Nominally the central government under Dezong controlled the two capitals and Guanzhong, but its usable manpower, revenue and legal capacity to move troops were all constrained by the regional governors: dispatching an army still ran through a petition-and-approval procedure in which every circuit supplied its own soldiers and grain, so the court could directly command only the capital garrisons and a few units around the capital, and the war in Hebei had to be fought with troops raised by the Hedong and Hebei circuits themselves, each led by its own jiedushi. On the Hebei side, Li Baochen, military governor of Chengde, held Hengzhou as his seat, with the jiedushi headquarters and the prefectural administrations running in parallel: he appointed his own officials, collected taxes and maintained a private guard, and his authority over his own army was close to absolute, the classic mid-Tang pattern in which military, fiscal and administrative power merged in the hands of one governor. Chengde was flanked by the circuits of Weibo, Youzhou and Ziqing, all of which refused the summons of the court, so the prefectures of Hebei had in practice become a source of soldiers and taxes owing obedience to the governors alone. After Li Baochen revolted, the court gathered an army under the title of Suppressor of Hebei, nominally commanded by Zhang Qiong, military governor of Zhaoyi, together with troops mustered from Hedong, Zhongwu and other places, yet in practice each circuit marched under its own commander, with no unified plan of operations and no single battlefield authority. Against them, Chengde could field not only its own army but also militia and local levies from the neighbouring prefectures and garrison troops holding the walled towns. In short, the Tang army had organisation and legitimacy but no coordination, while Chengde had cavalry and fortified strongpoints but no relief from outside: that structural asymmetry was the precondition for the defeat on the Huanshui.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物，多半在戰敗的一方。李寶臣是成德軍節度使，本姓張氏，早年效力於安祿山帳下，後歸唐朝，敕賜姓名李寶臣，以驍勇善騎聞名河朔；他在建中初年拒絕入朝，據恆州而叛，成為中唐藩鎮勢力最大的首領之一。朝廷最初派出的招討使是昭義軍節度使張瓊，他身兼招討使與本鎮節度使，名義上是河北討叛的總帥，實際上仍須與各道來軍協調，洹水敗後收拾散卒退保，是這場戰爭中唐方最直接的主事者，史料對統兵者的具體記載則有異辭，諸說並存。河北一線另有兩位起兵抗藩的地方大員：顏真卿以平原太守起兵募眾，是河北最早響應朝廷的義軍；魏博節度使田承嗣已死，其子承接魏博軍府，既不助唐，也不與朝廷正面為敵，河北諸將在朝廷與藩鎮之間看風向，正是雙方都不肯先耗盡的關鍵。德宗本人以削藩為志，卻在沒有把握的情況下屢發詔書，逼使方表態，激化衝突；名臣陸贄則反覆指出朝廷對河北用兵缺乏誠信、糧秣與持久作戰的準備，遣將必須假以專節、寬其文法，這些進言在當時未被採納。河北方面的李寶臣死後，諸子爭立又成新變數，最終朝廷改派河中節度使馬燧入河北，才在柏肆取得另一場勝利。
peopleEn: Most of the named figures attached to this war belong to the losing side. Li Baochen, military governor of Chengde, was born Zhang and had served in the household of An Lushan before coming over to Tang, where he was granted the name Li Baochen; he was famed throughout Hebei for his horsemanship and boldness, and in the early Jianzhong era refused to come to court, rebelling from Hengzhou to become one of the most powerful of the mid-Tang regional governors. The first commander the court sent against him was Zhang Qiong, military governor of Zhaoyi, who as Suppressor of Hebei was nominally the overall leader of the campaign, yet still had to coordinate with troops raised by other circuits; after the reverse on the Huanshui he gathered the stragglers and fell back, making him the Tang figure most directly answerable for this war, though the sources differ over the exact conduct of the command. Two others belong to the Hebei front: Yan Zhenqing, who raised a volunteer army at Pingyuan as prefect and led the earliest loyalist force in Hebei, and the dead Weiibo governor Tian Chengsi, whose son succeeded him in that army and neither aided the court nor openly confronted it, the governors of Hebei watching which way the wind blew, a posture that kept both sides from spending themselves prematurely. Dezong himself was set on reducing the power of the governors, yet issued edicts without securing the means to back them, forcing the other side to declare itself and sharpening the conflict; the minister Lu Zhi repeatedly argued that the campaign against Hebei lacked credibility, supplies and the capacity for a protracted war, and that any commander sent out needed exceptional authority, relaxed administrative rules and genuine trust. These remonstrances were not heeded. After Li Baochen's death, quarrels among his sons over the succession created a new opening, and it was not until the court switched to Hedong's governor Ma Xun that another victory, at Baisi, was obtained in Hebei.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬標槍並不在洹水的戰場上，它是共和末期至帝國時期羅馬軍團重裝步兵的標準投射兵器：槍頭為軟鐵製的空心管狀槍幹，插在木柄之上，全長約兩米而槍幹不足半米，槍幹一經撞上盾牌就會彎折並留在盾面，使中盾者無法拔出再用，一名持盾兵往往被釘在原地；前列士卒備重型標槍，每人腰後皮囊裝數十支輕型標槍，依令擲出形成數百步內的連續投槍雨，用以抬高敵盾、打散陣形，再由劍盾兵上前列陣決鬥。洹水一線的唐軍則完全沒有這類兵器：其投射火力來自弩與弓，步兵攜臂張弩，有效射程在百步上下，各營另備床子弩，配以長槍，射程可及數百步，交鋒之前往往先齊射數輪覆蓋；馬上用角弓與長弓，騎兵善奔射。冷兵器以長矛、方首槊與戟為主，配橫刀、儀刀；步軍披明光鎧，兜鍪與步盾、棹盾成列，長槊多植於木車欄上以拒敵騎衝撞，車前列拒馬，鹿角與木柵環繞宿營與營壘。攻城一方備飛雲梯、井車、撞車與石砲、木砲，壕溝與土壘是常規防線。河北藩鎮的屯田與鹽池收入足以支撐長期自守，唐軍糧秣則須自關中、河東運出，經太行諸陘轉運，車牛數量決定進攻的縱深。整體而言，羅馬標槍那種一次投射、難以回收的消耗邏輯與唐軍的箭矢、斷槊最為接近，武器形制則全然不同。
kitsEn: The Roman pilum on the card was not on the battlefield at Huanshui. It was the standard missile of the Roman legionary infantry of the late Republic and early Empire: a hollow, soft-iron tubular shank socketed on a wooden shaft, about two metres in total but less than half a metre of actual shank, which buckled and broke against a shield and stayed stuck there, so a man who was hit could not pull it free and use it again, and a shield-bearer was often pinned to the spot; front-rank soldiers carried heavy pila, with dozens of lighter ones in a leather pouch behind the belt, thrown on command in volleys covering several hundred paces, lifting enemy shields and breaking formation before the sword-and-shield infantry closed to decide the fight. The Tang army on the Huanshui front had no such weapon at all: its missile strength came from crossbows and bows, infantry carrying hand-drawn crossbows effective to about a hundred paces, each contingent also equipped with heavier bed crossbows firing long bolts out to several hundred paces, and the lines generally shooting several volleys before contact; on horseback they used composite and long bows, and the cavalry were adept at shooting from the gallop. Their close-combat arms were long spears, square-headed shuas and halberds, supported by cross-hilted and straight single-edged sabres; infantry wore Mingguan armour with helmets, shields and mantlets, long shuas were planted in the rails of wooden wagons to check charging enemy horse, and caltrops, wooden fences and abatis surrounded the camps and works. The besieging side brought flying ladders, well-carts, battering rams and stone and timber trebuchets, with ditches and earthen ramparts as the standard line of defence. The Hebei governors could sustain a long defensive war from their own tuntian and salt-pan revenues, whereas Tang grain and provisions had to be carried out of Guanzhong and Hedong and transhipped through the passes of the Taihang range, so the number of ox carts determined how deep the offensive could go. In short, the pilum's logic of a one-way throw that cannot be recovered is closest to the Tang arrow and the broken shua, but the weapon forms are entirely different.
tactics: 洹水之戰的具體經過，史料留下的只有骨架，細節多靠前後事推想，可以確定的是三件事。第一，唐廷的攻勢是一條由西向東、由北向南推進的斜線：昭義軍治潞州，據太行陘口，東出蒲陰陘、滏口陘，居高沿洹水上游南下，兵鋒直指成德軍治所恆州；一路要穿過磁、洺諸州的地界，這是河東、河北交界的地形險要處，也是糧秣最難維持的一段。第二，兩軍沒有大打會戰，而是在野外交鋒中以騎兵機動決定勝負：河北藩軍素以精騎著稱，戰法是先以輕騎散開掠擾、誘使唐軍分兵，再以突騎成建制衝擊唐軍側背與糧道，唐軍的突騎與步騎混編陣一旦被拉開，就在洹水兩側的縱深地帶失去相互支援；官軍潰敗之後，叛軍追擊不止，把整支隊伍衝散。第三，攻方的戰術缺陷在於沒有整體計畫：各道節度使各領本部兵，號令不一，進退失據，兵糧不統一籌措，先鋒與後援相距過遠，一遇挫敗便各自潰散。事後朝廷的反應也說明問題所在：詔令各軍退守，遣使宣撫，轉以招撫代替強攻，正是承認以當時的兵制與後勤無法在河北打贏一場攻勢戰。
tacticsEn: Only the skeleton of the Battle of Huanshui survives in the sources, and the details must be reconstructed from what happened before and after; three things can be stated with certainty. First, the Tang offensive ran on a diagonal from west to east and north to south: Zhaoyi's seat at Luzhou lay in the Taihang passes, and the army came east through the Puyin and Fukou passes, holding the high ground above the upper Huanshui and pressing down on Hengzhou, the seat of Chengde; the route crossed the territory of Ci and Ming prefectures at the junction of Hedong and Hebei, the most difficult ground and the stretch where supply was hardest to keep. Second, there was no set-piece engagement: the outcome was decided in open country by cavalry manoeuvre. The Hebei forces were famous for their elite horse, fighting by scattering light riders to harry the Tang line and draw it apart, then striking with formed shock cavalry at the flanks and against the baggage train; once the Tang shock cavalry and mixed foot-and-horse formations were pulled apart they lost mutual support in the deep ground on both sides of the river, and when the government army broke the rebels pursued without pause and scattered the whole force. Third, the attacker's tactical flaw lay in the absence of any overall plan: each circuit marched with its own troops under its own commander, orders were inconsistent, advances and withdrawals uncoordinated, supply was not centrally raised, vanguard and rear were too far apart, and the first reverse sent every contingent fleeing on its own. The court's reaction confirms the diagnosis: the troops were ordered to stand fast, envoys were sent to make terms, and coercion gave way to conciliation, an admission that the existing command system and logistics could not win an offensive campaign in Hebei.
data: 這一場戰爭留下的數字很少，必須分清哪些可以核對、哪些不可知。可以核對的是地理與建置：成德軍節度使治恆州，領恆、冀、趙、深、德諸州；昭義軍節度使治潞州，領澤、邢、洺、磁諸州，磁州正在洹水上游，洹水自太行山東麓流出，經磁州、臨漳東南流，至安陽一帶匯入漳水，磁州至匯口約二百餘里；由潞州取蒲陰陘、滏口陘東出，抵磁州一線約數日至十數日軍程，恆州又在洹水東北約二百里。建中初年朝廷曾議於諸州置團練使，年份諸說並存，一說建中三年，河北各州因此有常備的州兵與團練可以徵發。無法核對的是兵力與戰果：兩軍的出動兵員、斬首數與唐軍損失，舊唐書與資治通鑑都只寫大敗與潰散而不列數字，諸家注本亦未補充可靠統計；史載李寶臣精騎強於步卒，但官軍與藩軍的騎步比例、弩具數目都無記載。可用的時間錨點是：建中二年李寶臣起兵拒詔，洹水接戰在建中三年春，詔討與接戰的具體月份諸說不一，其後同年冬李寶臣病卒，諸子爭立；建中四年十月涇原兵變、德宗出奔奉天，馬燧在柏肆擊敗李惟岳。洹水至恆州約二百里、至魏州治所約百餘里這組距離，說明唐軍深入敵境已達二百里，供應線拉得極長。
dataEn: Few numbers survive for this war, and it is necessary to separate what can be checked from what cannot. What can be checked is geography and administration: the Chengde military governorship sat at Hengzhou and covered Heng, Ji, Zhao, Shen and De prefectures; Zhaoyi sat at Luzhou and covered Ze, Xing, Ming and Ci prefectures, Ci lying on the upper Huanshui. The Huanshui flows out of the eastern foothills of the Taihang range, past Ci and Linzhang, and joins the Zhangshui near Anyang, roughly two hundred li from Ci to the confluence; the march from Luzhou through the Puyin and Fukou passes to the Ci line took between several days and a fortnight, and Hengzhou lay about two hundred li further to the east of the Huanshui. The court discussed establishing tuanlian commanders in the prefectures in the early Jianzhong era, the year being disputed, one account giving Jianzhong 3, so the prefectures of Hebei could raise permanent local troops and militia. What cannot be checked is strength and results: neither the Old Book of Tang nor the Comprehensive Mirror gives the numbers of troops deployed, of enemy dead or of Tang losses, but simply records that the army was defeated and broke up, and no reliable statistics are added by the commentators. The sources do record that Li Baochen's strength lay in cavalry rather than infantry, yet give no figures for the ratio of horse to foot or for the number of crossbows. The usable time anchors are these: Li Baochen rose and refused the summons in Jianzhong 2; the clash on the Huanshui came in the spring of Jianzhong 3 (782), the exact month of the edict and of the fighting being disputed; Li Baochen died of illness at the end of that year, and his sons and captains then fought over the succession; in Jianzhong 4 (783) the Jingyuan troops mutinied in October, Dezong fled to Fengtian, and Ma Xun defeated Li Weiyue at Baisi. The distance figures, about two hundred li from the Huanshui to Hengzhou and about a hundred li to the seat of Weizhou, show that the Tang army had pushed two hundred li into enemy territory, stretching its supply line to breaking strain.
cause: 打起來的原因是中央的削藩志與河北藩鎮早已超出朝廷控制範圍的正面碰撞。德宗大曆十四年（779）即位以來，初行兩稅法、整頓度支，銳意削藩，但中央財力單薄，能直接支配的兵力有限，目標自然落在河北。河朔諸鎮的節度使多由父祖在安史之亂中的兵變、拒命與朝廷失控中得位，到建中年間成德、魏博、淄青、幽州已各自管轄州縣數十年，自置官吏、徵收賦稅、蓄養牙兵，朝廷的任命早已淪為一道需要藩鎮配合的手續。李寶臣本人的經歷正是這一格局的縮影：他本姓張，早年為安祿山帳下健兒，後歸唐朝，累授成德軍節度使，賜姓名李寶臣，掌軍近二十年，把成德經營成世襲的藩鎮。起兵的直接由頭是朝廷遣使宣詔、催令入朝並整頓軍鎮，詔使被拒，李寶臣與其將議定抗拒；朝廷不願容忍藩鎮坐大，於是下詔集合各道兵討之，張瓊受命為招討使，洹水之戰就是這道詔書的第一次軍事兌現。德宗需要一場看得見的勝利來鞏固聲望，資深老臣陸贄卻指出朝廷在河北既無糧秣、又無持久作戰的準備，遣將必須假以專節、寬其文法，這些意見未被採納。河北方面的算計同樣清楚：出仕等於交出軍府與地盤，固守城池與陘口則代價甚小而朝廷難近，兩邊都清楚一場決死戰對自己不利，於是起義成了一場以政治表態為主的角力，偏偏遇上河北正在壯大的野戰兵團。
causeEn: The war came out of the collision between a central government determined to curb the regional governors and a Hebei aristocracy that had already outgrown any effective control from the capital. From his accession in 779 Dezong had pressed administrative and fiscal reform, including the two-tax law, and had been set on reducing the power of the governors, but the court's finances remained thin and the troops at its disposal few, so the targets of the policy were naturally the Hebei governors. Many of those governors had taken their circuits through mutiny, refusal of orders and the collapse of central authority during the An-Shi rebellion, and by the Jianzhong era Chengde, Weibo, Ziqing and Youzhou had governed their prefectures for decades, appointing officials, levying taxes and holding armed guards, while the court's own appointments had degenerated into a formality that the governors merely had to nod at. Li Baochen's own career is the pattern in miniature: born Zhang, a former guard in the household of An Lushan, he came over to Tang, was advanced to military governor of Chengde and granted the name Li Baochen, and for close to twenty years turned the circuit into a hereditary principality of his own. The immediate trigger was the court's attempt to make the governors come to court and tighten the supervision of the circuits; the envoys carrying the edicts were not received, and Li Baochen consulted his captains on resisting. The court would not tolerate a governor sitting astride the marches, so it ordered troops mustered from the several circuits, appointed Zhang Qiong as Suppressor of Hebei, and the battle on the Huanshui was the first military cashing of that edict. Dezong needed a visible victory to shore up his prestige, while the veteran Lu Zhi argued that the court had neither grain nor the capacity for a protracted war in Hebei and that any commander sent out must be given exceptional authority and relaxed rules. Those remonstrances went unheeded. On the Hebei side the arithmetic was just as clear: submission meant surrendering the army and the country, while holding the walled towns and the passes cost little and kept the court at arm's length; both sides knew that a battle to the death would not suit either, and so the rising became a contest fought mainly for political display, until a campaign launched for effect met a field army that was still growing on ground of the governor's choosing.
impact: 洹水之敗是唐德宗削藩政策第一次真正的挫敗，影響遠及半個世紀。短期看，朝廷在河北的軍事信譽崩塌：各鎮節度使由此判定中央不能以兵自衛，於是詔書不再被當作必須執行的命令；李寶臣因大勝而氣焰更盛，河北諸鎮不僅不助唐，反而各自加緊城防與兵備，進表時多已不循舊例用臣字。直接的政治後果是削藩戰線全面停滯，德宗改行招撫，恢復李寶臣的節度使與封邑，承認河朔三鎮對州縣的實際控制，河朔藩鎮的半獨立局面由此固化。制度上，這場敗仗也暴露了唐軍在河北作戰的結構性難題：兵由各道自領、糧由各道自備，朝廷沒有能單獨調動的戰略預備隊，此後歷次用兵只能倚靠朝廷最信任的將領，如馬燧、李愬，以既有藩鎮身份就近用兵，兵權與軍鎮結合得更深。更遠的一層是唐廷整體處境的惡化：河北用兵牽制了關中有限的精兵，而西北吐蕃、劍南段子璋的叛亂同時起火，調度更加捉襟見肘；建中四年十月涇原兵變、德宗出奔奉天，表面上與河北無關，實則是同一條因果鏈的下游，禁兵盡出而京師無備，削藩的折騰最終反噬中央自身。史家也由此常把洹水之役視為中唐藩鎮割據定型的起點之一，河北三鎮此後或歸或叛，直至唐末都沒有真正解決。
impactEn: The defeat at Huanshui was the first real reverse of Dezong's policy of reducing the governors, and its consequences ran for half a century. In the short term the court's military credit in Hebei collapsed: the governors concluded that the centre could not defend itself in the field, and edicts ceased to be treated as commands that had to be obeyed. Li Baochen, inflated by victory, grew more arrogant; the other Hebei circuits not only refused to assist the court but reinforced their own walls and garrisons, and their memorials increasingly dropped the courtly formula of the humble servant. The immediate political effect was that the whole reduction-of-the-governors front stalled. The court resorted to conciliation, restored Li Baochen's governorship and investiture, and acknowledged the de facto control of the three Hebei circuits over their prefectures, fixing the semi-independent character of the region. Institutionally, the defeat exposed the structural difficulty of fighting in Hebei: soldiers were raised and grain supplied by the circuits themselves, and the court possessed no strategic reserve it could move on its own. Every later campaign therefore had to be fought by the governor the court trusted most, Ma Xun, later Pei Li, later Li Su, using the armies of the circuits in his own right, which fused military command and the governorship still further. At a greater remove, the overall position of the court deteriorated: the war in Hebei tied down the few reliable troops in Guanzhong while the Tibetans pressed on the northwest and the revolt of Duan Zizhang flared in the southwest, stretching the central command ever thinner. The Jingyuan mutiny of October 783 and Dezong's flight to Fengtian look unconnected with Hebei, yet they lie downstream on the same causal chain: with the palace guards sent out and the capital undefended, the campaign to curb the governors finally turned back on the centre itself. Historians accordingly treat the battle at Huanshui as one of the starting points of the settled pattern of mid-Tang separatism; the three Hebei circuits would thereafter submit or rebel as it suited them, and the problem was not genuinely solved before the dynasty fell.
result: 結果是攻方完敗、戰局被凍結在原地。官軍在洹水一線的野戰中潰散，招討使張瓊收攏散卒退保，討叛的第一次軍事嘗試以失敗告終；李寶臣沒有被消滅，反而以勝勢穩住成德，繼續以成德軍節度使的名號控制冀、趙、深、德諸州，並且拒絕入朝。李寶臣本人在建中三年末病卒，諸子與部將爭奪繼承，成德軍內部隨即分裂，又給了朝廷第二次機會：朝廷改派河中節度使馬燧入河北，建中四年在柏肆一戰擊敗李惟岳，李惟岳與其兄弟相繼死於亂軍，成德軍一度易主，但河朔割據的大格局並未改變，節度使的兵權與財權仍歸掌鎮者，唐廷對河北的實際控制僅止於羈縻二字。回頭看，洹水之戰的勝負並非偶然：攻方把河北當作可以速戰速決的外線，卻沒有為跨越太行、深入二百里的攻勢準備專一的指揮、統一的糧秣與可靠的偵察，也沒有估計到藩軍以騎兵與城寨為依托的持久抵抗；守方則以逸待勞、以整待散，把朝廷的急躁變成自己的時間。於是這場戰爭的真正結果是，唐廷承認自己無法用武力解決河朔，而河北藩鎮也明白，中央的每一次強行推進，仍須以自己的節度使印為前提。
resultEn: The result was a complete defeat for the attacker and a freezing of the situation in place. The government army broke up in the open field on the Huanshui, and the suppressor Zhang Qiong gathered the stragglers and fell back; the first military attempt to put down the revolt ended in failure. Li Baochen was not destroyed but stabilised himself at Chengde on the strength of the victory, continued to hold the governorship and its title over Ji, Zhao, Shen and De, and still refused to come to court. Li Baochen himself died of illness at the end of Jianzhong 3 (782); his sons and captains then fought over the succession and Chengde split internally, which gave the court a second opportunity. The court now sent Hedong's governor Ma Xun into Hebei, and in Jianzhong 4 (783) he defeated Li Weiyue at Baisi; Li Weiyue and his brothers were killed in the ensuing disorder and Chengde changed hands, but the larger pattern of separatism remained, the military and fiscal authority of the governor continued to belong to the man who held the circuit, and the court's effective control over Hebei amounted to little more than a nominal acknowledgement. Looking back, the outcome was not accidental. The attacker treated Hebei as an outer line to be won quickly, yet had prepared neither a single command, a common supply system nor reliable scouting for an offensive that had to cross the Taihang range and advance two hundred li into enemy country, and had not reckoned with a resistance based on cavalry and fortified towns. The defender, in turn, waited at ease, met the enemy formed with the enemy scattered, and turned the court's impatience into time on its own side. The true result of the battle was therefore this: the Tang court admitted that it could not settle Hebei by force, and the Hebei governors learned that even the centre's occasional forays still had to be premised on the governor's own seal.
